lessons.title: Ratio and proportion
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB National Syllabus, Mathematics, Level III (Classes 5-6) — to be checked against the official text
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Share a quantity in a given ratio.
Solve direct proportion problems with the unitary method.
reviewNotes: The existing word-problems lesson also uses the unitary method; overlap is deliberate (revision).
Inverse proportion is introduced only informally.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Ratio
blocks.md: A **ratio** compares two quantities of the same kind. If a class has 12 girls and 18 boys, the ratio of girls to boys is 12 : 18. We simplify it by dividing both numbers by their HCF (6): 12 : 18 = 2 : 3. The order matters: boys to girls is 3 : 2.

blocks.caption: Sharing 56,000 FCFA in the ratio 3 : 5.
blocks.alt: A bar cut into 8 equal boxes. The first 3 boxes are blue and the other 5 are yellow. Text says one part is 7,000 FCFA.

blocks.title: Sharing in a ratio
blocks.md:
1. Add the parts: 3 + 5 = 8 parts.
2. Find one part: total ÷ number of parts.
3. Multiply by each ratio number.
4. Check: the shares must add up to the total.

blocks.title: Direct proportion (unitary method)
blocks.md: When one quantity doubles, the other doubles too. First find the value of **one** unit, then multiply. If 5 kg of rice cost 4,500 FCFA, then 1 kg costs 4,500 ÷ 5 = 900 FCFA, and 8 kg cost 8 × 900 = 7,200 FCFA.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Sharing the total by the **ratio numbers** (3 and 5) instead of by the **number of parts** (8).
- Giving the answers in the wrong order.
- Using direct proportion when it is **inverse**: more workers means **fewer** days.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Share 56,000 FCFA between Ada and Bih in the ratio 3 : 5.
blocks.answer: Ada gets 21,000 FCFA and Bih gets 35,000 FCFA.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: 5 kg of rice cost 4,500 FCFA. How much do 8 kg cost?

objectives: Add, subtract and multiply amounts of money in FCFA.
Work out the change, a total bill and the best buy.
Plan a simple budget and savings.
reviewNotes: Banknote denominations quoted (1,000 / 2,000 / 5,000 / 10,000 FCFA) and 'coins' are given in general terms; check that they match the notes and coins in circulation.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Money in Cameroon
blocks.md: In Cameroon we use the **franc CFA** (FCFA). We use notes (for example 1,000, 2,000, 5,000 and 10,000 FCFA) and coins. **Total cost = unit price × quantity**. **Change = money given − total bill**. A good habit: estimate first, then calculate exactly.

items.text: 1 note of 5,000 FCFA = 5 notes of 1,000 FCFA

blocks.caption: Three FCFA notes and the rule for a total.
blocks.alt: Three rectangles shaped like notes, marked 1,000, 2,000 and 5,000. Under them are two lines of text about notes and the total.

blocks.title: Best buy
blocks.md: To compare two offers, find the **price of one** item in each offer. The offer with the lower price per item is the best buy. Example: 3 pens for 1,200 FCFA is 1,200 ÷ 3 = 400 FCFA each; 5 pens for 1,900 FCFA is 380 FCFA each: the second offer is better.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Forgetting a line of the shopping list when you add.
- Counting the change from the wrong note.
- Comparing the **total** prices of offers with different quantities: always compare the price **of one**.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: At Mokolo market, Mama Joy buys 3 kg of tomatoes at 600 FCFA per kg, 2 loaves of bread at 450 FCFA each and one bottle of oil at 1,250 FCFA. She pays with a 5,000 FCFA note. What is her change?

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: A pupil saves 1,500 FCFA each week. In how many weeks will she have 18,000 FCFA?

lessons.title: Profit, loss, discount and simple interest
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB National Syllabus, Mathematics, Level III (Classes 5-6) — to be checked against the official text
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Calculate profit, loss and percentage profit or loss.
Calculate a discount and a sale price.
reviewNotes: Interest rates and amounts are only for practice, not real bank rates. Check that the syllabus asks for simple interest with time in years only.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Profit and loss
blocks.md: The **cost price** (CP) is what a trader pays to buy goods. The **selling price** (SP) is what he sells them for. If SP is more than CP: **profit = SP − CP**. If SP is less than CP: **loss = CP − SP**. The percentage is always taken on the **cost price**: percentage profit = (profit ÷ CP) × 100.

blocks.caption: Cost price, selling price, profit and loss.
blocks.alt: Two boxes labelled cost price and selling price. Below, three lines say how to find profit, loss and the percentage.

blocks.title: Discount and simple interest
blocks.md: A **discount** is a reduction of the marked price: discount = marked price × rate ÷ 100; sale price = marked price − discount. **Simple interest**: I = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is the money saved or borrowed, R the yearly rate in % and T the time in years. The **amount** is P + I.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Dividing the profit by the **selling** price instead of the **cost** price.
- Using months for T: the rate is **per year**, so change months to years first (6 months = 0.5 year).
- Forgetting to add the interest to the money saved when the question asks for the **amount**.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: A trader buys goods for 8,000 FCFA and sells them for 10,000 FCFA. Find his percentage profit.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Find the simple interest on 50,000 FCFA at 6% a year for 3 years, and the amount.

lessons.title: Averages: mean, median, mode and range
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB National Syllabus, Mathematics, Level III (Classes 5-6) — to be checked against the official text
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Calculate the mean (average) of a set of numbers.
Find the median, the mode and the range.
reviewNotes: Median with an even number of values and the range: confirm they are in the Class 6 syllabus (enrichment otherwise).
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: The mean (average)
blocks.md: **Mean = total of the values ÷ number of values.** Example: the marks 12, 15, 9, 14 and 10 add up to 60. There are 5 pupils, so the mean is 60 ÷ 5 = 12. The mean can be a number that is not in the list.

blocks.caption: Marks of five pupils: the mean is 12.
blocks.alt: A bar chart of five pupils called Ada, Bih, Che, Dina and Eko. Their marks are 12, 15, 9, 14 and 10.

blocks.title: Median, mode and range
blocks.md:
- **Median**: the middle value when the numbers are in order. With an even number of values, find the mean of the two middle ones.
- **Mode**: the value that appears **most often**.
- **Range**: the biggest value minus the smallest value.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Finding the median **without** putting the numbers in order first.
- Dividing the total by the wrong number of values.
- Mixing up the mode (most frequent) and the mean.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Four numbers have a mean of 8. A fifth number is added and the mean becomes 9. Find the fifth number.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Find the median and the range of 2, 10, 4, 6.
steps: There are 4 values, so the median is the mean of the two middle ones: (4 + 6) ÷ 2 = 5.
